name: Seasats
note: Per-company dossier. Every field carries the source it came from and the date it was retrieved. Nothing here is inferred; where a fact is absent it is listed under gaps rather than estimated.

identity.description_by_company: Rugged self-righting USV operating in sea states up to 6, with collision avoidance, GPS-denied navigation and redundant communications for global reach.

axis_evidence.escort: Quickfish can protect the perimeter of vessels and infrastructure, intercepting and escorting anything that enters their space.
axis_evidence.escort_mission_list: MDA, ASW, sonar surveys, harbor security and HVU escort.
axis_evidence.commercial: Missions completed for defense, science, and commercial customers around the world.
axis_evidence.uncrewed: All three products are uncrewed surface vessels.

reclassified.reason: The escort and security axes were recorded false. seasats.com names HVU escort and harbour security as intended missions, so both are true on the company's own wording.

rounds.date_basis: Article published 2026-02-18 says the round was announced 'yesterday'.
rounds.stated_use: Expand production of its small uncrewed surface vessels.

contracts.date_basis: Article of 2026-02-18 states the award came 'in October'; naval today of 2026-03-20 places it in 2025.

contracts.instrument: APFIT (Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies)
contracts.customer: US Navy and US Marine Corps, joint
contracts.scope: Ramp production of the Lightfish and fund R&D on the other USVs.

platforms.name: Lightfish
platforms.share_of_business: CEO states all substantial business is on Lightfish, roughly 95% of focus.

platforms.name: Quickfish
platforms.endurance: operates for days; completed an 8-day continuous autonomous sea trial
platforms.role_by_company: Tactical and fast-response operations; protect the perimeter of vessels and infrastructure, intercepting and escorting

platforms.name: Heavyfish
platforms.role_by_company: MDA, ASW, sonar surveys, harbor security and HVU escort
platforms.status: in development as of 2026-02-18; expected in the water later that year

proof_points.claim: Iridium and Starlink communications with onboard AI
7,500-mile autonomous trans-Pacific voyage, San Diego to Japan
proof_points.when: stated in Feb 2026 as 'last year', so 2025

quotes.text: Funding helps us move faster and do a lot of things a lot quicker. Maritime is quite competitive right now, and there are a lot of people vying for space, so it made sense to do the raise.
Quickfish can protect the perimeter of vessels and infrastructure, intercepting and escorting anything that enters their space.

articles.title: Seasats Aims to Boost USV Production after $20M Series A
articles.author: Barratt Dewey
key_points: $20M Series A led by Konvoy Ventures, with Shield Capital and Techstars.
Lightfish about $250,000 a unit; Quickfish about $500,000.
Quickfish described as an interceptor USV, over 35 knots.
Heavyfish still in development at time of writing.

articles.title: Seasats Awarded $24M in Department of War APFIT Funding to Accelerate Fielding of its Autonomous Surface Vessels
key_points: $24M APFIT award to accelerate fielding of its autonomous surface vessels.

articles.title: Seasats Unveils The Quickfish: a High-Speed, Long-Endurance Autonomous Surface Vessel Proven in US Navy Exercise
key_points: Performance led to an $89M SBIR Phase III IDIQ supporting NIWC Atlantic and USMC USV efforts.

articles.title: Seasats Raises $20 Million To Increase Production Of Small USVs
key_points: Series A proceeds to expand production of small uncrewed surface vessels.

articles.title: Seasats: Quickfish USV completes 8-day continuous sea trial
key_points: Places the $89M SBIR Phase III in 2025, followed by the $24M APFIT award.

articles.title: L3Harris and Startup Seasats Accomplish Milestone in Proving Resilient, Distributed Maritime Autonomous Operations
key_points: Joint milestone in distributed maritime autonomous operations.
Lightfish operates autonomously for up to six months.

articles.title: Seasats company profile
key_points: Lightfish ~12 ft, Quickfish 20 ft, Heavyfish 35 ft as described here; these lengths differ from the Tectonic figures and from the company site.
CEO quoted that roughly 95% of focus is Lightfish.
Heavyfish described as a stretched Lightfish that does not need an expeditionary force to carry it off a beach.
articles.caution: Undated profile. Its platform lengths conflict with other sources; recorded here but not treated as authoritative.

values.value: Lightfish ~12 ft, Quickfish 20 ft, Heavyfish 35 ft

conflicts.resolution: Unresolved. The company site publishes weight and speed but not length.

gaps: No confirmation that Heavyfish entered the water; last statement was 'expected later this year' as of February 2026.
No commercial shipping customer is named anywhere. Every named customer is a defence one: US Navy, USMC, NIWC Atlantic.
No escort service offering, pricing or contract is published - escort appears as a platform capability, not a service sold to shipowners.
Founding year not confirmed by a primary source.
Total funding 'over $40M' is a press characterisation; the components before the Series A are not itemised.
